title: két éve and két évvel ezelőtt: saying ago

sections.title: Past tense plus a time, and you get ago
sections.content: You know *két éve* from *óta* (a2-52): with a present-tense verb it means "for two years", as in *Két éve itt lakom* ("I have lived here for two years"). With a past-tense verb the same phrase looks back to a moment: *Két éve költöztünk ide* means "We moved here two years ago". The tense of the verb decides the meaning. For "ago" there is also a fuller form: a time word with *-val/-vel*, then *ezelőtt*: *két évvel ezelőtt*.

sections.title: the same words, a different tense
rows: I have lived here for two years.
I moved here two years ago.

items.english: We went hiking three days ago.
I did sport a week ago.
Two years ago I worked in Budapest.
They had a picnic in the park an hour ago.

sections.content: The short form is the time word with *-a/-e/-ja*: *órája, napja, hete, éve*. The full form uses *-val/-vel*, which assimilates: *nap* gives *nappal*, *hét* gives *héttel*, *év* gives *évvel*, *óra* gives *órával*. *Három napja* and *három nappal ezelőtt* are two ways to say the same thing, so use one or the other, never both together.
